notes: A clean eight-bullet ladder with one real judgement call at the end. Bullet 2 ('she will then ask for a Stardust pebble') is the outcome of bullet 1, not an action, so the two merge into one talk. Bullet 7's target is the problem: the page calls it 'the glowing pebbles targetable location' and then its own sub-bullet admits the spot is NOT glowing and tells you to 'target around at (I-5) and pay attention to your target names in order to find the spot' -- which is the wiki saying, in as many words, that it does not know the entity's name. 'Glowing Pebbles' would resolve as a key, but it is a description in a sentence, not a name the page gives, so the target is none/null and the step keeps its zone and grid, which is the part a player actually needs. That costs step 7 its marker and nothing else: the Stardust pebble is still the evidence, so the ladder moves off (I-5) the moment you have it. Jugner Forest (S) resolves as zone 82 and is a genuinely different zone from present-day Jugner Forest (104), so the past steps are zoned to the (S) form. The 'Level: 30+' header is a plain level gate on any job.

notes: Three real bullets and a wall of destinations. Bullet 3 is an OR over eighteen Geomagnetic Founts -- you attune ONE, and the sub-bullets are a menu with EXP prices, not eighteen things to do. The schema has no one-of, so the eighteen share a group: a group draws all its members at once, which is exactly the map a player wants here, and the note on every member says only one is needed. That is the whole reason this quest is flagged or_branch_modelled rather than left as a single zone-less fount row that would match everywhere. Every one of the eighteen zones resolves, and each keeps its own grid, so the choice is presented honestly instead of being collapsed. The Temporary geomagnetron is a KEY item (id 2158, there is no item of that name) and it is granted by Darcia at step 1, so it is step 1's evidence -- the header lists it under Quest Reqs, but you do not bring it, she hands it over. It is deliberately NOT listed on the turn-in: the page never says whether attuning consumes it, and a required hold that is already gone would leave the hand-in permanently un-ready. The founts do carry it as a required hold, because you plainly cannot attune a device you do not have.

notes: Six bullets, six real actions, and one bullet that is nine tenths tactics. Bullet 5 is the whole battlefield: examine the Forbidding Portal for a cutscene, examine it AGAIN to enter, then fight. It is kept as ONE step on the portal rather than split into examine + fight, because the page never names the opponent -- it says only 'one humanoid who uses all sword weapon skills' -- and never names the battlefield zone, so a separate fight rung would have no target, no mobs and no zone, which is noise. Everything the page does say about the fight is in that step's note. The last sub-bullet of 5 is the tell that the Commander's endorsement is CONSUMED on entry: 'should you lose this battle, speak to Gentle Tiger for another', which is also why the endorsement is a required hold on the portal and not on any later step. Bullet 4 is a zone-entry cutscene, so it is a travel step whose destination carries the endorsement as evidence. The trailing line 'if you are working on missions then return to Fate in Haze' is a pointer to a WotG mission, not a step in this quest. Fame reads 'Wings of the Goddess', which is not one of the nine fame regions, so it gates nothing and only raw is kept.

The opponent is one humanoid the page never names, so no mob is recorded: all sword weapon skills, frequent double attacks, Mighty Strikes at 50%, then a monster two-hour animation and an AoE Temblor Blade that petrifies. It randomly picks a player and wipes that player's enmity, and magic -- nukes and enhancing especially -- draws disproportionate hate. Trusts are allowed; item level 119 gear trivialises it. Losing consumes the endorsement and you must ask Gentle Tiger for another.

notes: A cutscene chain with exactly one fight and no observable state anywhere -- no key item, no quest item, nothing dropped -- so every evidence field is null and the ladder rests entirely on position. That is the honest reading; reaching for the reward (Chanoix's Gorget) as evidence would break the reward rule. Bullets 5 and 6 are the same Toad's Footprint clicked twice, so they merge the way Divine Might's blank target does, with the spawn recorded on the merged step. Bullet 8 is a THIRD click on the same tracks after the win, which the page really does call for, so the unmarkable fight sits between two examines on the same object because the page puts it there. Bullet 7's five helper frogs -- Mikiruru, Mikiluru, Mikirulu, Nikilulu, Mikilulu -- are deliberately NOT recorded as mobs: they are near-identical strings that look like wiki transcription artefacts, they are not targets you are sent to kill (one of them cannot be killed at all), and putting five markers on them would be worse than the note that names them. Only Poroggo Casanova is a real target. Bullet 2's 'secret entrance' is a zone line out of Aht Urhgan Whitegate, so it is a travel step to Wajaom Woodlands with the departure grid in the note. The header's fame 'Treasures of Aht Urhgan' resolves to the Aht Urhgan region.

notes: Three bullets and a twenty-row table, and the table IS the walkthrough -- bullet 2 says 'speak to all twenty (20) NPCs in the below chart' and nothing else, so dropping the table would leave a quest with one instruction and no destinations. The twenty share a group: nothing in the page orders them, a strict ladder would mark Npopo alone and then nothing until you happened to walk past him, and all twenty drawn at once is the map this quest actually is. Five of them are listed under 'Windurst Waters (North)', which is not a zone -- North and South are two halves of Windurst Waters (238) -- so they are zoned to Windurst Waters and keep their own grids. The Green Sentinel badge is step 1's evidence and must be held for the whole tour; it is listed as a required hold only on the hand-in, where it is exchanged, rather than repeated on all twenty talks. The Green invitation card is NOT evidence: it is the header's Reward, so it proves the quest is over, not that a step is done. The 'After the walkthrough: Notes' section is two post-quest bullets -- Naja Salaheem paying Imperial currency for the card, and Alib-Mufalib's 300 gil teleport to Aht Urhgan Whitegate -- both after this quest ends, so neither is a step. Shantotto and Nanaa Mihgo appear here as ordinary tour stops.

notes: Two markers is the whole quest. Bullet 2 -- invite a second player and change to a job at level 15 or below -- is a precondition, not a place you go, so it folds into the Hunting Bear step's source bullets and note rather than becoming a rung with no target and no zone. Bullets 3 and 4 are travel to and talk to the same galka in the same zone, so they merge; a separate travel step to North Gustaberg would put a second marker on top of the first. The level requirement is an inverse cap -- you must be level 15 or BELOW -- which the schema's level gate cannot express (it means a minimum), so gates.level stays null rather than gating this quest to level 15+, which would be exactly backwards. The party-of-two requirement is likewise unmodellable. The 'After the walkthrough: Notes' section is trivia and patch history: the cutscene showing party members, watching it again at the Goblin Footprint, and the June 2015 update that cut the requirement from six players at level 5 to two at level 15. None of it is a step.

steps.note: the galka near the waterfall; the Survival Guide drops you at the Outpost, which is fairly close. You must arrive with a party of at least two, on a job at level 15 or below -- Trusts and Adventuring Fellows do not count, Level Sync does, and you only need to be synced at the moment you speak to him. Anyone under level 20 walks, since mounts need 20.
